To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of a graphene based wearable electrooculogram (EOG) acquisition and processing system with an integrated automatic detection of eye movements (Ems).

1) Graphene based dry electrodes have been successfully used for the acquisition and analysis of electrooculography, and 2) A new method to detect eye movements has been proposed and experimentally demonstrated using a wearable eye tracker.

graphene based textile electrodes can be successfully employed for EOG signal acquisition with a high correlation with the wet Ag/AgCl electrodes, and that the proposed algorithm can be used to detect EMs with a high success rate, thus paving the road to a new era of wearable EOG devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of graphene based electroconductors for the development of dry, gel free, flexible textile electrodes for EOCG sensing, the development and characterization of a wearable EOG based eye tracker and the development of a novel automatic EM detection algorithm.

the development and demonstration of a wearable eye tracking system based on graphene embedded textile electrodes and a custom designed embedded hardware with real time processing and streaming of data over Bluetooth.
the design, fabrication and characterization of novel graphene based dry textile electrodes for electrooculogram acquisition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented work is the first demonstration of the feasibility and applicability of graphene embedded textiles as a wearable EOG sensor for eye tracking applications.
the presented work demonstrates the applicability and the potential of graphene textiles for wearable and dry EOG based sensing, processing and remote control of objects.
this work presents for the first time a novel, wearable, dry, graphene based, flexible, and textile based EOG sensor and its application toward EM detection and HCI.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

graphene based textiles are an attractive alternative for conventional electrodes and can be used for EOG sensing, and that the developed eye tracker is capable of accurately detecting eye movements in real time and can be used to control a variety of applications in the domain of HCI.

the proposed system is a step toward a new generation of soft, wearable, flexible, textile based, dry electrodes for EOG sensing and processing, and the development of wearable devices with embedded EM detection capabilities for the control and monitoring of the user activity.
graphene textiles are an attractive alternative to Ag/AgCl electrodes and that the developed system can be used as an EM sensor and as an HCI control device.
The main takeaway from our work is that
graphene embedded textile electrodes may be used as dry, flexible and conformal alternatives to conventional "wet", pre-gelled electrodes for the acquisition of electrooculogram (EOG) signals.
the use of dry graphene based electrodes in conjunction with a custom designed wearable eye tracking device can be a viable alternative to wet electrodes in the domain of wearable electronics.

graphene embedded dry electrodes can be used to measure EOGs with high correlation to conventional wet Ag/AgCl electrodes and the resulting EOGs can be reliably used to detect and classify different EM patterns.
